further_description: Fixed O&M of 1.5%/year of the investment, the technology-data CH4 (g) pipeline value (same as the H2 (g) pipeline in 2050, from Danish Energy Agency Technology Data for Energy Transport 2021, datasheet H2 140). Investment of a new 36-inch onshore pipeline. As an H2 pipeline it costs (3.20 MEUR/km pipe + 93 MWe/1000 km compression * 4.0 MEUR/MWe) / 4,700 MW = 760.0 EUR/MW_LHV/km: pipe and compressor costs from EHB November 2023 Table 1 (https://ehb.eu/files/downloads/EHB-2023-20-Nov-FINAL-design.pdf), taken as 2023 EUR; throughput and compression capacity at 100% capacity from EHB June 2021 Table 35 (https://natrangroupe.com/sites/default/files/2021-06/European-Hydrogen-Backbone-report-June2021.pdf). For natural gas it is scaled by 0.884 / 1.1 to 610.8 EUR/MW_LHV/km, from Transition Accelerator, The Techno-Economics of Hydrogen Pipelines (https://transitionaccelerator.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/The-Techno-Economics-of-Hydrogen-Pipelines-v2.pdf): the same pipe carries 88.4% as much energy as H2 as it does as methane (LHV, Section 4.2 Table 4.1), and an H2 pipeline costs 1.1 times a natural gas pipeline (Section 5.1 Table 5.1). Divided by 1.11 (methane HHV/LHV, 55.5/50.0 MJ/kg) to 550.2 EUR/MW_HHV/km, and converted at 1.0817 USD/EUR (2023 average, FRED AEXUSEU) to 2023 USD

4%/year FOM of 29.948 2025 EUR/kW_gas investment (PyPSA-Eur H2 compressor 93.437 EUR/kW_H2 divided by 3.12, the volumetric energy density of methane over hydrogen), times 1.1306 USD/EUR (2025 average, FRED AEXUSEU) and divided by 1.06 (CPI-U 2025/2023) to 2023 USD; per MW of injection capacity.
